title: Random record operators: the generic leading-order witness geometry

key_results.statement: In both ensembles the record vector is the first column of the record operator, $\lvert u_h\rangle=\sum_{a=2}^{d_c}(K_h)_{a1}\,e_a\in\chi^\perp$, and the $u_h$ ($h=1,\dots,n$) are independent and identically distributed.
GUE: for $z_{h,a}=(K_h)_{a1}$, $a=2,\dots,d_c$, the real and imaginary parts $\operatorname{Re}z_{h,a}$ and $\operatorname{Im}z_{h,a}$ are i.i.d. $N(0,s^2/2)$.

GUE: for every unit vector $e\in\chi^\perp$, $E\lvert\langle e\vert u_h\rangle\rvert^2=s^2$ and $E\langle e\vert u_h\rangle^2=0$, so $u_h$ is a circularly symmetric complex Gaussian vector with mean $0$ and covariance $s^2\mathbb 1_{\chi^\perp}$.
GUE: the density of $u_h$ on $\chi^\perp$ in real coordinates is $p(u)=(\pi s^2)^{-(d_c-1)}\exp(-\lVert u\rVert^2/s^2)$, which does not depend on the choice of $e_2,\dots,e_{d_c}$.
GUE: for $h\ne h'$, $d_0(h,h')^2\overset{d}{=}s^2\chi^2_{2(d_c-1)}$, with density $x^{d_c-2}e^{-x/(2s^2)}/\bigl((d_c-2)!\,(2s^2)^{d_c-1}\bigr)$ for $x>0$.
GUE: $E\,d_0^2=2(d_c-1)s^2$, $\operatorname{Var}d_0^2=4(d_c-1)s^4$ and the relative standard deviation of $d_0^2$ is $1/\sqrt{d_c-1}$; all depend only on $s$ and $d_c$.
GUE: $\dim_0=\min\bigl(n-1,\,2(d_c-1)\bigr)$ almost surely, so the bound (5.14) is attained.
GOE: $u_h\sim N(0,s^2\mathbb 1)$ in the real span $\chi^\perp_{\mathbb R}$ of $e_2,\dots,e_{d_c}$, with density $(2\pi s^2)^{-(d_c-1)/2}\exp(-\lVert u\rVert^2/(2s^2))$, independent for different $h$.
GOE: for $h\ne h'$, $d_0(h,h')^2\overset{d}{=}2s^2\chi^2_{d_c-1}$, with density $x^{(d_c-3)/2}e^{-x/(4s^2)}/\bigl(\Gamma(\tfrac{d_c-1}2)\,(4s^2)^{(d_c-1)/2}\bigr)$ for $x>0$.
GOE: $E\,d_0^2=2(d_c-1)s^2$, $\operatorname{Var}d_0^2=8(d_c-1)s^4$ and the relative standard deviation of $d_0^2$ is $\sqrt{2/(d_c-1)}$; all depend only on $s$ and $d_c$.
GOE: $\dim_0=\min(n-1,\,d_c-1)$ almost surely; for $n>d_c$ this is strictly below the bound (5.14), so the GOE does not attain it there.

Unified form, with $m=2(d_c-1)$ (GUE) or $m=d_c-1$ (GOE) and $\sigma^2=s^2$ (GUE) or $2s^2$ (GOE): the $u_h$ are i.i.d. isotropic Gaussian points in an $m$-dimensional Euclidean space, $d_0^2\overset{d}{=}\sigma^2\chi^2_m$, $E\,d_0^2=2(d_c-1)s^2$, the relative standard deviation of $d_0^2$ is $\sqrt{2/m}$, and $\dim_0=\min(n-1,m)$ almost surely.

Regime (a), $n$ fixed and $d_c\to\infty$: with $\bar d=E\,d_0(h,h')$, for $0<\epsilon\le1$ and $m\ge32/\epsilon^2$, $P\bigl(\max_{h\ne h'}\lvert d_0(h,h')/\bar d-1\rvert>\epsilon\bigr)\le16\,n(n-1)/(m\epsilon^2)$; hence all normalized distances converge to $1$ in probability and the normalized configuration tends to a regular simplex.
Regime (b), $n\ge m+1$ (in particular $n>m+1$): $\dim_0=m$ almost surely, with $m=2(d_c-1)$ for GUE and $m=d_c-1$ for GOE, independent of $n$; the value is fixed by the medium and not by $n$.

definitions.name: Gaussian unitary ensemble of record operators with scale s
Gaussian orthogonal ensemble of record operators with scale s
Number of places of the part a, n ≥ 2
Real dimension of the record-vector space

open_issues: GOE(s) is defined relative to the basis (e_a) with e₁ = χ, so it uses a real structure in which χ is real, which is not part of the description data; the GOE results are invariant under real orthogonal changes of e₂, …, e_dc, and the GUE results do not depend on the basis at all.
Distances that share a place, such as d₀(1,2) and d₀(1,3), are correlated through u₁; only the union bound was needed in (7.14), and the joint law is out of scope.
All statements are leading order in λ; finite λ and non-Gaussian ensembles are out of scope.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions: s carries the unit of K_h, so d₀² ∝ s² and Var d₀² ∝ s⁴ in (7.5)–(7.6) and (7.9)–(7.10), while chi-square variables and relative deviations are dimensionless.

Qubit medium, d_c = 2: for GUE the u_h lie in a complex line ≅ ℝ², m = 2 and dim₀ = 2 for n ≥ 3, and |z_h − z_h'|² is exponential with mean 2s², that is s² times chi-square with 2 degrees of freedom, as (7.5)–(7.6) state; for GOE the points lie on a line and dim₀ = 1 for every n ≥ 2, matching (7.9) and (7.11).

s → 0: E d₀² = 2(d_c−1)s² → 0, so every d₀ → 0 and all places merge into one point, consistent with K_h → 0 leaving no record by (5.10); for every s > 0, dim₀ and the law of every ratio of distances do not depend on s.
